measurement: RQ6 §4.5.1 M11 - ISR partial regeneration cost
methodology: crates/loom-fic/src/bin/isr_bench.rs, native (not browser), release build, median of 20 reps per n_sections value. Re-measured after the 2026-07-24 same-day static-markup-collapse optimization (codegen.rs's try_render_fully_static + DomOps::append_static_html) was added mid-session in response to a design question about compile-time template emission.
note_on_rigor: Smaller/narrower than RQ1's full paired-bootstrap protocol - median-of-20 only, no CI, native timing not browser timing. Sufficient to show the scaling shape, not a publication-grade benchmark.

three_variants.monolithic_naive: pre-optimization codegen shape - one DomOps::create_element/append_static_text call per static node
three_variants.monolithic_optimized: post-optimization - all static sections built as one plain Rust String (no DomOps calls) then inserted via one DomOps::append_static_html call, matching what codegen.rs now actually generates for a fully-static subtree
three_variants.widget_only: Island-style independent re-render of just the dynamic widget, never touching the surrounding n_sections content at all

interpretation: The 2026-07-24 static-markup-collapse optimization (matching docs/02's originally-stated 'compile-time HTML template string' design, previously unimplemented) cuts the monolithic path's marginal per-section cost by roughly 7-14x (naive ~0.19-0.22us/section -> optimized ~0.015-0.03us/section). This substantially narrows the ISR partial-regeneration case for Islands. HOWEVER the optimized monolithic path still scales linearly with n_sections (still has to build+copy all the static bytes on every regeneration), while widget_only stays flat regardless of n_sections (Island's independent render never touches those bytes at all - true O(1), not just 'cheap O(n)'). At n_sections=50000 the optimized-vs-widget-only ratio is still roughly 30-70x, down from naive's ~400x. Conclusion: the compile-time optimization is real and worth having on its own merits, but it does not eliminate the structural ISR advantage Islands have - it only reduces its magnitude.
